subject: Culture
title: ANZAC Day
description: Learn ANZAC Day in one minute.

hook.text: Australia and New Zealand celebrate ANZAC Day—a military defeat. Gallipoli in 1915 was a disaster.

buildup.text: Thousands of young soldiers died in a failed campaign against the Ottoman Empire.

discovery.text: The defeat forged national identity. Australians saw themselves as distinct from Britain for the first time.

twist.text: Turkey also honors Gallipoli—as a victory. The same battlefield is sacred to both sides.

climax.text: ANZAC Day proves nations sometimes build identity from loss, not triumph.

punchline.text: A defeat can define a nation more than a victory.

quiz.question: What 1915 event does ANZAC Day commemorate?

details.summary: ANZAC Day (April 25) commemorates the 1915 Gallipoli landing — a catastrophic military defeat that paradoxically became the founding myth of Australian and New Zealand national identity.
details.whyItMatters: ANZAC Day is unique among national holidays — it commemorates a devastating military failure rather than a victory. This reveals how nations construct identity from sacrifice as much as triumph.
takeaways: ANZAC Day commemorates the failed Gallipoli campaign of 1915
Dawn services reflect the dawn landing at Gallipoli
It became a founding myth of Australian and New Zealand identity

faq.question: Why do Australians celebrate a military defeat?
faq.answer: The Gallipoli campaign (1915-16) cost over 11,000 Australian and 2,700 New Zealand lives with no strategic gain. But the courage, mateship, and sacrifice of the ANZACs became the founding story of national character for both young nations, which had only recently federated.

faq.question: Is ANZAC Day controversial?
faq.answer: Increasingly. Critics argue it glorifies war, sidelines indigenous Australians' military service, ignores the campaign's futility, and excludes women's contributions. Debate continues about whether reverential commemoration of Gallipoli prevents honest reckoning with war's costs.
